verdict: CHANGES_SUPPORTED_BUT_NOT_APPLIED: one automated loss does not prove M6 impossible and does not justify a global combat nerf. Current source nevertheless creates a concrete M6-only opening-pressure defect: eight independently firing fleet defenses are already inside their 1,800-stud firing radius at spawn, all have fireTimer=0, and ground/naval fire bypasses the airborne one-threat cap. The observed health losses are multiples of Normal's six-damage hostile hit and are compatible with repeated fleet-defense volleys, but shooter identity was not captured, so attribution remains a strong source-based inference rather than direct observation.

normalActI.airFire: Ordinary aircraft require 450 < range < 1700, sufficient nose alignment, no active evade, their own fireTimer<=0, and the flight-wide gate. Initial aircraft fireTimer is 7+0.4*index seconds. Windup is 2.4 seconds. With 11 live aircraft, Normal flightGate is 22/1.5 = 14.67 seconds and threatCap is 1, so ordinary aircraft cannot create eleven simultaneous missile threats.
normalActI.missiles: Hostile speed 580 studs/s, life 7 seconds, fuse 32 studs, steering 1.6, damage 6 per hit on Normal. A non-ace aircraft reloads after 10 seconds.
normalActI.groundNavalFire: Every enabled SAM, AA GUN, FLAK, GUN, or component-less naval hull independently decrements fireTimer and launches inside 1,800 studs when timer<=0, then reloads at 8 seconds. This path has no windup, aim test, evade suppression, or shared threat cap. Ground/naval enemies are constructed with fireTimer=0 and all phase-zero groups enable together.
normalActI.targeting: M6 has no protected actor. ac04ProtectedTarget returns undefined, so every hostile missile targets the player aircraft. Protected-target combat does not explain this loss.
normalActI.damageConsistency: 100->70 is five six-damage hits; 70->58 is two; 58->40 is three. These exact multiples match Normal hostile missile damage. The final 40->0 digest omits intermediate samples and cannot establish the number or origin of fatal hits.

combatTrace.timingInference: All eight listed defenses can launch at the first combat step, then again near 8 and 16 seconds if still in range. Four disclosed evades could plausibly clear part of the initial volley; later volleys plus the first aircraft windup/launch can plausibly produce the 12/15/18-second loss samples. Straight-line times ignore missile steering and aircraft movement and are inference only.
combatTrace.shipFireScope: Tanager own-barrel regression and double-hull/deck-fire fixes remain source-fixed/native-fixture-passed. This investigation does not claim actual Tanager fire was observed. supportedDiscrepancies: Geofon becomes an abstract missile shooter although the original unit table lists no Geofon weapon.
Eight fleet defenses begin in immediate firing radius with synchronized zero timers; no consulted reference supports this opening synchronized volley.
The implemented 11-aircraft opening count is supported only by a Normal aggregate header, not by evidence that all 11 should be simultaneously active or aggressively engage at time zero.

The original-reference strategies emphasize fast ground/naval attack and ignoring initial fighters; the automation instead locked F-14 1 and scored zero targets before death. That is a strategy mismatch, not proof that aircraft balance itself is defective.

causalAssessment.legitimateDifficulty: M6 is a long, hazardous air-to-ground score attack with many fighters and SAM-equipped ships. References explicitly warn about SAMs and recommend speed, altitude, passes, and resupply. Some pressure is legitimate.
causalAssessment.automationPolicyWeakness: The only observed attempt selected an F-14, produced zero target kills, and used four evades without logged threat timing. Reference strategy says to ignore opening fighters, run full throttle toward surface objectives, climb, and respond to missile direction. A generic dogfight-oriented pilot is not a valid playability oracle for M6.
causalAssessment.spawnTargetingDefect: Independently of pilot quality, immediate synchronized fire from eight nearby fleet defenses is source-verifiable and unsupported by references. Geofon's abstract fire is a concrete weapon-host mapping defect. These are narrower than a global difficulty problem.
causalAssessment.confidence: High for source mechanics and geometry; medium-high that fleet defenses materially caused the loss; low for exact shooter/hit attribution because per-projectile telemetry and sortie capture are absent.

recommendation.smallestCorrection: First remove abstract fire from M6 naval hulls and allow only explicitly authored weapon components/ground defenses to shoot. This removes Geofon and both missile-boat hull attacks while preserving Raven SAMs, Tanager guns, cruiser/destroyer components, terrain cover, the own-barrel fix, all aircraft behavior, damage, ranges, and global difficulty. Then stagger the initial M6 component-defense timers so five nearby deck weapons do not launch on the same first step. Do not change global hostile damage, fighter count, lock range, or threat cap from this single run.
